paragraphs.text: "As long as I stand, so will your cause."
"You were saying?"
"I appreciate things that exceed expectations." —Mizzix
"Violence is the food it craves. Feed it if you dare." —Doriel, mentor of Mistral Isle
To Jin-Gitaxias, perfection is not a goal, but a process.
Even when the flesh grows cold, knowledge waits in the bones for a master to release it.
The terrors of the Underworld travel alongside those who return to the mortal realm.
When the winds blow out of the abyss, death is the only harvest.
"Did you have a nice nap?" —Liliana Vess
"May all the cairns of Jund be toppled." —Meren of Clan Nel Toth
Her hunger will not be denied.
Its wings shimmer with dreams absorbed from its enemies.
"Fate is not as fixed as you might think."
"Behold astronomy's contribution to war." —Fennor Rhyl, starcaller
Every movement is a summons—even your screams.
"Those who do not submit will be consumed."
His roots reach deep and grip hard.
"My skills are wasted here." —Juruk, Kalonian tracker
He speaks directly into his supplicants' minds using fiery words that inflame their thoughts and incite their passions.
"Does Teysa think me blind to her scheming? Ambition runs in our family."
"Our revered ancestor Seshiro gave us wisdom greater than poison and fangs."
The clicks and buzz of the undercity proclaim him the incarnation of decay.
"I'd rather see the guilds contend together with words in the halls of power, than in the streets with swords." —Jace Beleren
Infinite possibilities contained in a finite space.
"I gazed once into that light. Now it burns in my mind, forever denying me rest." —Riku of Two Reflections
"United, our roar will level mountains."
Though giants are mortal, they live so long and on such a grand scale that many small folk don't believe they ever truly die.
Not all silences are easily broken.
"We thought the clouds had moved from the night sky. Then the night sky moved, and the horizon grew wings." —Josuri
"The numbers of Nyxborn among us have swelled. Is this a sign of the gods' favor, or does it portend something else?"
"What we knew as Emeria, Ula, and Cosi were not divine beings at all, but a cruel trick, and a grave error." —*The Invokers' Tales*
"In our war Heliod gave mortals some favor, yet other times he withheld aid. Are we still no more than game pieces to him?" —Polyxene the Doubter
Light's champion in the stronghold of darkness.
"Why keep such trinkets? They only add weight to your travels."
She shepherds mysteries and dust as others would a flock of sheep.
"Belief is the strongest mortar."
When the vaults are empty, everyone is rich.
"I am the purifier, the light that clears all shadows." —Seal inscription
When Asha left Bant, she ensured that the world would have protection and order in her absence.
It serves a justice higher than the whims of the gods.
A blazing sun that never sets.
The corruption stirred the heavens above, awaking a shining champion.
"I prefer loyalty to be a matter of respect, not of magic. But one does what one must." —Kaalia of the Vast
"You can come back once you've learned some manners—and figured out how to reconstitute your physical forms."
The wills of mortals shift as the tide ebbs and flows.
"I'll leave subtlety to the rich."
"The Origin Query will wait. We must ensure we survive to return to it." —Pelyus, vedalken ordinar
Weather is more predictable than the Izzet.
The mizzium-sphere array drove her mind deep into the thought field, where only the rarest motes of genius may be plucked.
"I've come to reclaim what is mine. And you, Greven, are mine." —Volrath
A single lie unleashes a tide of disbelief.
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
"This is a sacred duty. Master Beleren's trust has bought an eternity of my loyalty."
"We've merged your life essence with that of several creatures at once. You're welcome." —Speaker Trifon
"Your deed cannot be undone. You, however, can be." —Agosto, Azorius imperator
"I give them dreams so wondrous that they hesitate to return to the world of the conscious." —Garild, merfolk mage
After a hundred failed experiments, Urza was stunned to find that common silver passed through the portal undamaged. He immediately designed a golem made of the metal.
"The seas are vast, but the skies are even more so. Why be content with one kingdom when I can rule them both?"
Knowledge fills the mind of a fool and opens the mind of the sage.
"To fill your mind with knowledge, we must start by emptying it." —Barrin, master wizard
"Don't worry, your death will be as informative as possible." —Gorghul, augur of skulls
The waters of wisdom are as dust in the mouth of one who thirsts for power.
Knowledge demands sacrifice.
"We must all make sacrifices for the good of Innistrad." —Sorin Markov
The travelers were warned to watch out for children on the road.
His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.
Crippling fear precedes it. A foul stench accompanies it. Death follows in its wake.
Gods can be appeased. Demons, however . . .
"Never forget that the life you've built can be undone by a single loose thread." —Perisophia the philosopher
Merchants of the Underworld trade in coins of clay. Gold serves another purpose.
"Sometimes the grave does not wait for death before relishing its feast of flesh and bones." —Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours
A drop of humanity for a sea of power.
"The final stage of the illness: delirium, convulsions, and death." —Phyrexian progress notes
"I believe many worlds will bow to Phyrexia. Mirrodin is merely the first." —Sheoldred, Whispering One
Death is no excuse to stop working.
"Death is no excuse for disobedience." —Liliana Vess
"A basilisk's gaze is effective, but disposing of physical remains is a tiresome task. It's far more discreet to dissolve one's victim entirely." —Szadek
If you're looking for it, it's available. The question is how much you're willing to pay.
"Die. But die knowing that your pathetic life will yield a great bounty for me." —Zul Ashur, lich lord
Giants share nothing but their fury.
"We train for the improbable, like lightning striking the same place twice, or striking everywhere at once." —Nundari, Sea Gate militia captain
When the moon rises and the bloodlust takes hold, nothing matters but the kill.
Her mind was quite gone, yet she spoke nothing but truth.
"You'll bend to my will—with or without your precious sanity."
They fell screaming into the depths of the chasm like so many pebbles tossed down a well.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
It is unwise to insult the god of the forge. It is also unwise to stand near anyone else who has insulted him.
"If you live on a giant's back, there's only one individual you'll ever need to fear." —Gaddock Teeg
"Oh sure, they buy a lot of ale, but I always find myself needing to rebuild after the giants have paid a visit." —Belko, owner of Titan's Keg tavern
The knights see a mighty quarry. The dragon sees breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
Its open mouth is a furnace blast that blisters the skin. Its smoking fists are meteors that split the earth.
"Where will you run when I punish you with the very ground you flee on?" —Nicol Bolas
Boggarts constantly strive to outdo each other with the things they bring back to the warren, each hoping the exploit will become as well-known as those of Auntie Grub.
A hundred generations has he mentored, a hundred armies has he crushed beneath his feet, yet only a hundred words has he ever spoken, each more revered than a hundred books.
The power of a waterfall. The fury of an avalanche. The intellect of a gale-force wind.
He cares not for the disasters his storm brings as long as his path ahead is clear.
Beauty is in the eye of the exploder.
"Listen to the roar! Feel the thunder! The Immersturm shouts its approval with every bolt of lightning!"
"Obey!"
It sees shaped stone and carved wood as mutilations.
Massive, mindless, and imbued with one terrible purpose.
"From a tiny sprout, the greatest trees grow and flourish. May the seeds of your mind be equally fruitful."
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Its blood is life. Its body is growth.
"An indrik's howl has destructive power much subtler than that of its crushing foot. The sound is mundane, but inaudible vibrations scatter and sunder magical contrivances." —Simic research notes
"They put bars on these noble beasts and then wonder why werewolves target our towns."
"The land grows only where the kami will it." —Dosan the Falling Leaf
"Give up these unnatural weapons, these scrolls. Heart and mind and fist are enough." —Zyd, Kamahlite druid
His work determines who is remembered and who feeds the worms.
The land knows no difference between the graves of commoners and nobles.
The ohran viper is not cold-blooded. Its veins course with the same antigelid venom used to kill its prey.
Nature doesn't walk.
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
There were no tombstones in orochi territory. Slain warriors were buried with a tree sapling, so they would become a part of the forest after death.
The first satyr to wake after a revel must search for the site of the next one.
The juiciest prey is that which grows lazy, thinking itself beyond the reach of danger.
"You may enter, but leave those lifeless things of your world behind." —Modruni, maro-sorcerer
Left to itself, nature overflows any container, overthrows any restriction, and overreaches any boundary.
She stands as a living symbol of the natural world and an enemy of the forces that threaten it.
"I will fight only the way nature intended—and nature intended us to win."
Each flower identical, every leaf and petal disturbingly exact.
Every branch a crossroads, every vine a swift steed.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
Plate mail, the skin of the chest, the rib cage, the heart—all useless against the mage who can reach directly for the soul.
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."
"Let the rest of Ravnica sneer. One way or another, they all end up in the undercity." —Jarad
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.
"The enlightenment I never found in etherium I have found traced in the coatl's scales." —Ranalus, vedalken heretic
He lurks in the undercity, eager for the corpse haulers to unload their rotting cargo.
Its fangs are in your flesh before its hiss leaves your ears.
"We are all decaying, always in a state of near-death. One moment without breath and we begin to break down." —Cevraya, Golgari shaman
Keranos is a fickle god, delivering punishment as readily as prophecy.
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.
Coins of the Underworld are shaped from clay funerary masks.
"When something dies, all things benefit. Well okay, just our things." —Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
"Look beyond, to the vascular awareness that all life is a map to greater knowledge." —Momir Vig, *Biomancy*, vol. I
It hears and answers every orison across Shadowmoor.
She follows the old tributaries built when merrows still shaped the tides.
Losing his possessions distressed him, but the lack of limbs was strangely liberating.
Selkies call to a sea they never swam, in a tongue they never spoke, with a song they never learned.
"In case of fire, treachery, citywide riot, political upheaval, or worldwide societal collapse, break glass." —Cluestone inscription
"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride." —Agrus Kos
Forged by divine hands to wander mortal realms.
The Phyrexian death machine awoke, its coldsteel heart imbuing it with sinister new power.
As Serra was to learn, the peace and sanctity of her realm were as fragile as glass.
"It reflects the purity of Mirrodin-that-was." —Koth of the Hammer
Only the Eldrazi mind thinks in the warped paths required to open the hedrons and tap the power within.
"Gods don't die. They merely slumber." —Ayli, Kamsa cleric
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
"A crafter must imbue her weapon with part of her soul—something the Phyrexians are incapable of doing." —Melira
"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?" —Jhoira, master artificer
A symbol of power and wealth, the only commodities that matter to the Orzhov.
The form of the sigil is just as important as the sigil itself. If it's carried on a medallion, its bearer is a master. If it's tattooed on the body, its bearer is a slave.
"If that brain can't figure out the secret of the serum, then add more brains." —Rhmir, Hand of the Augur
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
The mind is a beautiful bounty encased in an annoying bone container.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
"I have attuned the staff to your screams so that only I may benefit from your pain." —Volux, disciple of Nin
"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared." —Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
When wielded by a true believer, it matters little whether the sword is a relic or a replica.
"Stop thinking like an artificer, Urza, and start thinking like a father!" —Rayne, chancellor of the Tolarian Academy
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Even a fragment of a powerstone contains within it not just energy, but space—vast dimensions trapped in fragile crystal.
The arbiter Galanda Feudkiller judges Lorwyn's squabbles from a lofty perspective.
It promises protection to those in need and proclaims a warning to any who would threaten Ravnican law.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.
Deserted, but not uninhabited.
Enter those who are starving and sick. You are welcome among the Swarm when the rest of Ravnica rejects you.
"I love what they've done with the place." —Liliana Vess
If it can't be had here, it can't be had on any world.
Enter those with the vision to create and the daring to release their creations.
"The unnatural pressures of life in this city are best withstood by lifeforms that adapt with unnatural swiftness." —Momir Vig
Enter to find wealth, security, and eternal life . . . for just a small price up front.
Once guarded by the Knights of the Reliquary, the tower stands now protected only by its own remoteness, its dusty treasures open to plunder by anyone.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
Enter and comprehend the perfection of orchestrated life.
Those who bring nothing to the temple take nothing away.
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
Nothing lives within it, yet there is life.
